stemMd: A fair coin is tossed four times. What is the probability of exactly one head?
explanationMd: There are 2⁴=16 equally likely sequences. Exactly one head can occupy any of four positions, giving four favourable sequences. Probability is 4/16=1/4.

distractorRationale.a: This counts one specific position for the head instead of four possible positions.
distractorRationale.c: This is the probability of a head on one toss, not the stated event.
distractorRationale.e: There are sixteen equally likely sequences, not five.
